negative_findings.description: Repeated Hungarian-language searches for a Barion press room / newsroom ('Barion sajtószoba', 'Barion Payment Zrt hírek sajtó') returned only integration tutorials, reseller pages and company-registry entries — no Barion-operated press-release index surfaced in search results.
negative_findings.result_summary: Barion's own announcement channel could not be pinned to a specific URL; PR appears to reach the market via Prim.hu, Portfolio.hu and FinTechZone instead. Not evidence the page does not exist — only that it is not search-discoverable from these queries.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Barion is one of the two most important independent HU PSPs; without a primary announcement feed, partnership signals must be picked up second-hand with a lag and lower fidelity.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian-language Revolut or Wise press room surfaced. Revolut HU branch news (MNB registration late 2025, migration of 2M+ clients, qvik and payment-request rollout, new transaction fees) was found only through Hungarian financial media (Portfolio, Világgazdaság, HVG, Economx, Infostart, Bank360, Biztosdöntés).
negative_findings.result_summary: Coverage is media-mediated rather than issuer-primary for the neobank actors in this cell.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Neobank moves into local rails (qvik, HUF accounts) directly reshape acceptance and merchant payment behaviour; a media-only pipeline risks missing technical/partner detail that press releases carry.

negative_findings.description: Searched explicitly for a Nexi-Euronet Hungarian ATM/POS acquiring partnership announcement; nothing of the kind was found. Both operate in Hungary independently.
negative_findings.result_summary: No such partnership evidenced. Recorded as a negative finding rather than inferred.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents a fabricated linkage entering the actor map.

negative_findings.description: For Wise's Hungarian presence, no Hungarian-language corporate or regulatory terminology beyond the generic 'fióktelep' surfaced; the only concrete artefact was a Hungarian branch registration reference and Wise's own hu-locale marketing blog (wise.com/hu/blog) which writes about competitors (PayU) rather than about Wise's HU partnerships.
negative_findings.result_summary: Wise HU is under-covered in this pass; local-language terminology for its acquiring/merchant activity may not exist because it has little merchant-acceptance footprint in HU.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Wise was named in the cell scope; its absence from acceptance-side sources may itself be the finding, but should be confirmed rather than assumed.

negative_findings.description: Portfolio.hu and Világgazdaság articles on Revolut/acquiring are partially paywalled; MNB Intézménykereső and GIRO's document library are behind query/filter UIs rather than static listings.
negative_findings.result_summary: Several of the highest-value sources need either metadata-only collection or form-driven fetching rather than simple crawling.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must budget for form interaction and for licence-safe metadata-only ingestion of paywalled press.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank-side acquirers other than OTP and Erste were not covered in this pass: MBH Bank, K&H (beyond one qvik PDF), Raiffeisen, UniCredit, CIB and Gránit — all of which either acquire directly or resell a PSP's terminal estate.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass over each bank's 'sajtószoba/sajtóközlemények' and 'kártyaelfogadás/POS terminál' product sections to complete the acquirer census.

coverage_gaps.description: Independent/softPOS and terminal-adjacent challengers were only touched via secondary coverage (Billingo x Global Payments softPOS). SumUp, myPOS, Viva.com, Revolut Reader and local ISO/distributors were not systematically searched.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search 'softPOS Magyarország', 'mobil kártyaelfogadás kisvállalkozásoknak', 'bankfüggetlen elfogadó' and enumerate challenger acquirers and their HU distribution partners.

coverage_gaps.description: No procurement/tender source was inspected. Public-sector acquiring and terminal contracts (Magyar Posta, Magyar Államkincstár, NÚSZ — all named as SimplePay partners) are typically awarded via published tenders.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add Közbeszerzési Értesítő / EKR and TED to the source set with payment-terminal and acquiring CPV filters; this is the strongest evidence-grade partnership source in the cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Case-study material is thin: no vendor case-study libraries, conference agendas or award submissions were captured beyond the OTP Mobil partner awards article and EkerNap.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Harvest case-study/referencia sections of Worldline HU, Global Payments HU, Nexi CE and Barion, plus FinTechShow and EkerNap agendas, where merchant deployments are named.

coverage_gaps.description: Several anchor facts found are historical (Global Payments/Erste 2014, Worldline-SIX 2018, GVH inquiry 2019); 2025-2026 partnership flow was captured mostly for Revolut and qvik.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run date-bounded queries (2025, 2026) per actor and monitor MNB Fizetési rendszer jelentés 2026 for updated acquirer concentration data.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language investor/analyst material on Nexi, Worldline and Global Payments was only lightly sampled; group-level results decks often break out CEE/Hungary volumes.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add the three groups' IR pages and quarterly presentations, filtering for Hungary/CEE segment disclosure.

brief: Hungary's acquiring/PSP landscape is unusually well documented from primary sources: an oligopolistic acquirer core (OTP Mobil/SimplePay, Global Payments HU via the Erste channel, Worldline/SIX, Nexi Central Europe, Euronet) that publishes aggressively in Hungarian on its own sites, wrapped by an authoritative regulator layer (MNB Intézménykereső for licences, MNB Fizetési rendszer jelentés for POS/acceptance counts, and the GVH 2019 sectoral inquiry into card acceptance) and by GIRO Zrt., which effectively maintains a live participant roster for instant payment and qvik. The richest partnership signal is not press releases but structural lists: SimplePay's technical-partner directory, GIRO's GIROInstant participant list, Ecommerce Hungary's 200+ member base and webshop-platform integration catalogues. Secondary Hungarian trade media — FinTechZone above all, then Portfolio.hu, Kosárérték and Prim — function as the pointer layer and are the practical substitute where a vendor has no discoverable newsroom (Barion, Revolut HU, Wise HU). Main remaining gaps are the non-OTP bank acquirers, the softPOS/challenger tier, and public procurement, which is where the largest Hungarian acceptance contracts are actually awarded.
